World Watch · design language · 28 Nov 2026

Porcelain

Black ink on white porcelain, with a whisper of lavender and blue. The icon is the Earth seen from 20° N 10° W. The white patch is everything Sentinel-2 can see from 786 km above Munich, and the black dot is Munich.

1 · The icon

Lighter tile, rounder Earth

The tile is now almost white, the globe is lit like a ball, and there is a dark twin for dark mode.

Light

White porcelain. Tailwind's violet-100 glows in from the top left and sky-100 from the bottom right, and both fade to white before the middle. The last tile used those two colours edge to edge.

Dark twin your pick

Zinc-950 tile with violet-950 and sky-950 whispers, a white globe, and the footprint as its negative. A white ball with a dark disc reads more like an eye than the light icon does. It stays clear at 16 px on a dark taskbar.

Planet alternative

The same black Earth as the light icon, outlined by its own atmosphere on a dark tile. It is the better picture at Dock size, but at 16 px on a dark taskbar the globe disappears into the tile.

More 3D

The globe is shaded as a matte sphere lit from the top left. A thin atmosphere glows along the sunlit edge, and the white footprint darkens towards the limb with it.

Sitting on the tile

The globe casts a soft shadow, tinted indigo-950, straight down onto the tile. The tile's rounded edge catches light along the top and turns faintly lavender along the bottom.

Same geometry

Nothing moved: the camera, the 786 km horizon and the pupil are computed exactly as in the mark you approved. From 32 px down a flat version takes over, with a bigger footprint and pupil.

Camera
Orthographic view from 20.0° N 10.0° W, so Munich sits up and to the right of the centre
Footprint
Sentinel-2's horizon at 786 km: arccos(R / (R + h)) = 27.1°, a cap 6,028 km across
Pupil
Munich at 48.137° N 11.575° E, radius 3.6 on the 64 grid (5.2 in the small version)
Tile
64 grid, corner radius 14. The globe has radius 26.5 (29 in the small version)
Rendered
Each pixel is ray-cast through the sphere in numpy and shaded in linear light. No 3D software is involved, so the shape stays exact

3 · Name and lockups

World Watch, set wide

Set in Mona Sans at 118 % width and weight 640, then turned into outlines so it never falls back to another font.

Space around itKeep a quarter of the icon's height clear on every side of a lockup.
SmallestIcon 16 px. The wordmark is 16 px tall in the app's top bar and never smaller than 12 px.
NeverTint the globe, put the icon on a photo without its tile, or set the name in another face.

5 · Type

A cockpit face and a court face

I picked four free faces, each made for a real job. A research pass checked 17 families: who drew each one, what it was made for, and its licence file. All four are SIL Open Font License 1.1 and on Google Fonts.

Headings, the name
Kharkiv · Now
Mona Sans

GitHub's typeface, drawn with Degarism and inspired by industrial-era grotesques. It has a width axis from 75 to 125 %. Headings use 112–118 %, so they sit wide like a map.

OFL 1.1 · Google Fonts · source
Everything you read in the app
RCH4934 over Kyiv
B612

Commissioned by Airbus with ENAC and the Université de Toulouse III, and drawn by Intactile DESIGN for cockpit screens. It was tested for map labels, waypoint lists and capitals mixed with digits, which is this app's job.

OFL 1.1 · Google Fonts · source
Codes and IDs
253400JT3MQWNDKMJE44
B612 Mono

The same cockpit family with every character the same width, used for LEIs, register numbers, transponder addresses and email addresses. Numbers do not need it: B612's own digits all share one width, so counts, times and coordinates line up in plain B612 and keep a narrow point and comma.

OFL 1.1 · Google Fonts · source
Printed reports and case files
Rosneft Deutschland Specimen
Redaction

Jeremy Mickel drew it for Titus Kaphar and Reginald Dwayne Betts' The Redaction (MoMA PS1, 2019), from Times and Century Schoolbook, the faces of US legal documents. Its numbered cuts are degraded like photocopied filings, and Redaction 50 Bold is our stamp.

6 · Devices

Four things that repeat

They come from the icon and from the subject: a footprint, a camera position, porcelain, and the stamp on a filing.

Horizon ring

The selected thing gets one thin ring, the way the footprint rings Munich. It is ink on light and white on dark, with a halo so it reads on any ground. Never a crosshair.

Seen from
44.2° N 36.0° E · zoom 3.2
28 Nov 2026 03:08 UTC
Seen-from line

Every map view and every report says where it was seen from and when. The icon says the same thing about itself.

Porcelain surface

Panels are white with 18 px corners, a hairline, a light top edge and a soft indigo-tinted shadow. No blur and no glass, which is cheaper for Safari over a moving map.

SpecimenConsent on fileSanctioned by LEINot verified
Stamps

Only in printed documents: Redaction 50 Bold in rose-700, slightly crooked, saying a fact about the file. Never on screen and never on the map.

White land, pale sea

The land is white and the sea is sky-50, so the porcelain panels float over the map the way the icon's Earth sits on its tile. In dark mode the land is zinc-900 on a zinc-950 sea.

Your symbols, solid

These are the 147 approved symbols, drawn solid with a white edge. They are smaller and calmer than in God's eye. News is ink dots sized by outlets, like newsprint.

What is thin

World aircraft are left out because the stored snapshot is 9 days old. No earthquakes fell inside this view in USGS's last day, and the USNI carriers are outside it.

11 · Sources

Where everything comes from

So the system can be checked, rebuilt and changed.

Colour and icon

Tailwind CSS v3.4.17 palette (src/public/colors.js, MIT). Anduril black #010101 from anduril.com's stylesheet, read in the earlier colour round.

The icon is rendered by our own numpy ray caster from the mark's exact geometry. The sources are in docs/brand/porcelain/.

Type

Mona Sans: GitHub and Degarism. B612 and B612 Mono: Airbus, ENAC, Université de Toulouse III and Intactile DESIGN. Redaction: Jeremy Mickel (MCKL).

All four are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, which was read in each project's OFL.txt. They load from Google Fonts here. The wordmark is outlined from Mona Sans at 118 % width and weight 640.

Data on the boards

App: GDELT Events and GKG, adsb.fi, Fintraffic Digitraffic (CC BY 4.0), DeepState, Launch Library 2 and Natural Earth outlines. All of it is the latest copy in the server's store, newest 28 Nov 2026 03:08 UTC.

Documents: GLEIF (CC0), Wikidata (CC0), OpenSanctions (CC BY-NC 4.0), XposedOrNot, Hudson Rock Cavalier, Gravatar, rdap.org and crt.sh. These were fetched 28 Nov 2026 12:36–12:38 UTC.

Not tested

Safari and real screens: everything was checked in headless Chromium only. The icon was not seen on a real Windows taskbar or Dock. There are no .ico or Icon Composer files yet.

B612 for long text is untried in the real app. The Redaction cuts are static fonts, and printing from the browser is untried.
